title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet: As the Abyss spread across the land of Oolacile, Knight Artorias arrived to halt its advance and confront Manus, as the Knight of Gwyn already had experience with fighting the Abyss and its creatures after the events of New Londo and his hunt for the Darkwraiths, and possessed a Silver Pendant that protected him from the Dark. However, Artorias's pendant was stolen by Oolacile's inhabitants and hidden behind an illusory wall, depriving Artorias of protection against Manus's dark sorceries. Together with his trusted companion Sif, Artorias faced Manus but his strength proved insufficient to defeat him, and he succumbed to the Abyss. Injured in the battle, Artorias used his Cleansing Greatshield to form a magic barrier that protected Sif from the Dark. Now corrupted to his soul by the Abyss and with his armor corroded, Artorias was left to fight alone and hold back the treacherous citizens of Oolacile.

title: Knight Artorias

Wounded in the battle, Artorias used his Cleansing Greatshield to form a magic barrier to protect Sif against the Dark. title: Knight Artorias
snippet:
Knight Artorias -  Dark Souls III - boss - lead 
 lead : **Knight Artorias** (騎士アルトリウス), also known as **Artorias the Abysswalker** or **Artorias of the Abyss**, is a boss in *Dark Souls*. He appears exclusively in the *Artorias of the Abyss* DLC named after him.

Artorias was previously a mentioned character in the base game, in which the Chosen Undead must acquire Artorias' ring by slaying his former companion, Great Grey Wolf Sif. He is also a mentioned character in *Dark Souls III*, in which he is known as the **"Wolf Knight"**, his real name seemingly lost to history.

title: Abyss
snippet: Knight Artorias famously traversed New Londo's Abyss and hunted the Darkwraiths therein. He was protected by the power of a magical ring, which he gained after making a covenant with the beasts there. The ring prevented him from being swallowed by the void, but it led to his sword becoming cursed. In recognition of his actions, he was awarded one of Anor Londo's treasures, a Silver Pendant that allowed him to repel Dark sorceries; eventually he traveled to Oolacile to combat the threat of Manus, the lord of the Abyss. He ultimately failed in his mission he was overtaken by the dark, leaving behind his companion Sif.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: A nation of humans freed from the shackles of the Darksign, in possession of an army empowered by their boundless Dark Soul, represented an unparalleled threat to the gods of Anor Londo, who branded the Darkwraiths diabolical enemies of man and of every living thing. Artorias, as one of the Four Knights of Gwyn, was sent to fight the dark soldiers of New Londo, being granted a Silver Pendant to deflect the Dark of the Abyss he would face. However this did not prove sufficient to cross into the Abyss of the Four Kings, and Artorias was forced to forge a covenant with the "beasts of the Abyss", obtaining a ring that would allow him to cross the Abyss, but also cursed his sword in the process. Artorias thus became known as the "Abysswalker" and hunted the Darkwraiths, but failed to eliminate the Four Kings and close the Abyss of New Londo. Following Artorias's failure, an agonizing and terrible decision was made in order to contain the Abyss: flooding the entirety of New Londo, despite

title: Knight Artorias
snippet:
Manus at one point kidnapped Princess Dusk of Oolacile and imprisoned her deep within the Chasm of the Abyss. His prized pendant eventually came under the possession of a Chosen Undead in the future; Manus, driven by his unrelenting search for his pendant, snatched the Undead from the future and brought them into the old Oolacile. There, the Chosen Undead encountered Knight Artorias, who had retained only the very last vestige of his sanity in the battle against the Abyss, still desperate to put down the corrupted creatures of Oolacile. During the fight that ensued between him and the Chosen Undead, Artorias succumbed to the Abyss entirely, and was finally defeated by the Undead.

Ciaran, who had arrived at the arena where Artorias was corrupted by the Abyss, also requested the Soul of Artorias from the Chosen Undead who had finally put an end to the knight's suffering, with the intention of paying proper respects to her passed dear friend.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: Artorias wore his distinctive azure-blue tassel armor as a symbol of pride and glory and brandished a greatsword and greatshield. Artorias was also a dear friend of Ciaran, his companion as another Knight of Gwyn. At one point Artorias met Sif, a great grey wolf, with whom he formed a deep bond. Artorias and Sif would brave the battlefields as companions; Sif even learned to fight with Artorias's greatsword, and acquired the power of his soul.

snippet:

The sword Sif carries in their mouth appears to be a replica of Artorias' sword. The sword also apparently changes size between the events of Artorias of the Abyss and the main game.

title: Knight Artorias

Sif survived the battle with Manus thanks to the intervention of the Chosen Undead. The wolf inherited Artorias's divine greatsword and the magical ring that had allowed the knight to cross the Abyss. The wolf settled in the forest where Artorias's tomb had been erected and, wielding his companion's sword in his jaws, continued to fight to guard Artorias's rest, slaughtering the numerous Undead who arrived with the intention of plundering the tomb of the legendary knight.

While the name of the "Wolf Knight" was seemingly lost to history, there were many who swore themselves into a new covenant with the goal of fighting Abyss's abominations. These warriors would come to be known as Farron's Undead Legion, The Abyss Watchers. It was said that the Undead Legion vowed to partake of "wolf blood", binding their souls into one that traced its roots to Artorias, the first Abyss Watcher, in an eternal mandate to hold back the tides of the Abyss. They imitated the fighting style of their first master, becoming known for their wild, ferocious style which employed the unusual combination of an ultra-greatsword and a parrying dagger.

title: Knight Artorias

snippet:

Without wearing the ring, it is impossible to survive the fall into the Abyss. Taking off the ring during the fight with the Four Kings will cause the player to be devoured by the Abyss. The Covenant of Artorias is one of the very few rings that do not carry over to NG+; players are required to kill Great Grey Wolf Sif every playthrough to obtain the ring and beat the game. This ring, when dropped, will end up in the chest behind Kingseeker Frampt after the player has quit and reloaded the game. title: Four Kings
snippet: A nation of humans freed from the shackles of the Darksign, and who not only began to understand the powers of their Dark Soul but had an entire army at their disposal that shared this power, represented an unparalleled threat to the gods of Anor Londo, who branded the Darkwraiths as diabolical enemies of man and of every living thing. For this reason, Artorias, one of the Four Knights of Gwyn, was sent to fight the soldiers of New Londo and was given a Silver Pendant to deflect the Dark of the Abyss in its magical forms. The events of the DLC are also related to the story of *Dark Souls II*, as Nashandra was born from a fragment of Manus' soul.

title: Lords
snippet:
One of Gwyn's four knights, Artorias, and his wolf companion Sif made a covenant with the beings of the Abyss that allowed him to traverse it, so that he could hunt the Darkwraiths. Artorias later arrived in Oolacile in an attempt to combat the spread of the Abyss, but was overcome and was forced to sacrifice his greatshield to save Sif. This left him unprotected from the Abyss, and he later became corrupted and driven to madness.

The Way of White was usurped by Gwyn's uncle, Lloyd, who also would start hunts against the Undead.

Eventually, the undead were corralled into several asylums to await the end of the world, for it is prophesied by Astora - who themselves inherited the prophecy from Frampt - that one day an undead will escape the prison and succeed Gwyn in linking the fire. At the same time, Kaathe preaches that this chosen has the opportunity to become the new Dark Lord and usher in the Age of Dark.

Artorias, along with Ornstein, Ciaran and Gough, thus formed the Four Knights of Gwyn; as a symbol of his association with the order, he was bestowed a magical ring with the wolf symbol, which strengthened his poise, making his fighting style with a greatsword more effective.

 wrath_of_the_abyss_buff : After Artorias has lost 1/3 of his health, he will start to use his Wrath of the Abyss power up. If left alone, he will do much more damage after he completes the power up for 90 seconds, potentially one-shotting the player. If the player can get close fast enough, they can Poise break him out of his charge up by dealing 90 Poise damage as his usual 130 Poise value is reduced during his buff animation. If the player doesn't do enough Poise damage fast enough, he will hit them with an area of effect blast attack that will knock the player on their back. The best bet is to use a decent Poise damage weapon and stop him from gaining his attack buff. If using a low Poise damage weapon, check the Poise Damage Values of your weapon to calculate the beast way to deal 90 poise damage to him via a combination of light and heavy attacks.

Following Artorias's failure, an agonizing and terrible decision was made in order to contain the Abyss: flooding the entirety of New Londo, despite the realization that countless lives would be lost along with its prosperous culture. For this task, sorcerers were called forth and the feat was accomplished without evacuating the city's civilians, sealing away the Four Kings, their Darkwraiths and the entire population with them. The victims were cursed and became Ghosts roaming the ruins of their country.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: Many years later during the Age of Fire, shortly after the fall of Izalith to the Flame of Chaos, a group of Dragon Knights serving Gwyn and led by Dragon Knight Gravis arrives in New Londo in an attempt to negociate assistance against Izalith, unaware that the Four Kings have been convinced to rebel against Gwyn. They are attacked by a group of Darkwraiths and Skeletons, who slay all but Gravis and hired mercenary Wurdow; as they prepare for a last stand, the two are rescued by Artorias, who decapitates all foes surrounding them. As Gravis expresses her surprise and gratitude, Artorias points them to the gate they had entered to silently order them to leave, and progresses deeper into New Londo alone.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet: Manus at one point kidnapped Princess Dusk of Oolacile—possibly after her rescue from a Golden Crystal Golem—and imprisoned her deep within the Chasm of the Abyss. In the meantime, his prized pendant came under the possession of Seath the Scaleless and then a Chosen Undead in the future; Manus, driven by his unrelenting search for his pendant, snatched the Undead from the future and brought them into the old Oolacile. There, the Chosen Undead put down the corrupted Knight Artorias and journeyed within the Chasm of the Abyss, where they finally defeated Manus and put him to rest. While Dusk was rescued in the process, she was driven by Elizabeth into thinking that she was saved by Artorias, preserving the legacy of the Wolf Knight. Nevertheless, Dusk came to recognize the Chosen Undead's similarity to the fabled knight, and developed doubts of her own as to her true savior.

A console version of the *Prepare to Die Edition* was also released at a later date. The DLC content is also automatically available in the Dark Souls Remastered Editions.

title: Lord's Blade Ciaran
snippet:
Lord's Blade Ciaran -  Dark Souls III - character - cut_content 
 cut_content : According to [https://youtu.be/ny5B9Hxn6KA?t=56 her cut dialogue], she would have reacted to the player owning a ring that belonged to Artorias, which was stolen by "a man in a long coat", likely the shady Marvellous Chester. She would then ask them if they'd be willing to hand it over to her. This sequence was replaced by her request to to be given his soul.

A potentially ominous interaction is revealed [https://youtu.be/irlXZqq5egY?t=27s in a cut dialogue] from Hawkeye Gough. He was meant to warn the slayer of Knight Artorias about Ciaran, citing her affection for the knight. This seems to imply that the assassin may have been intended to fight players for what they did to the Abysswalker, motivated by her feelings for him. In the final game, her love for Artorias is much less pronounced, and could even be seen as simple admiration.

Empowered by the legacy of Artorias, they became intensely strong and agile, fighting in a coordinated and sporadic pack akin to wolves.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: The Abyss Watchers established dominion over Farron Keep, the swampland once known as Oolacile or Darkroot Garden. Here they closely guarded what was once the Chasm of the Abyss, the cradle of Manus and a seedbed for Abyssal beasts; these headquarters would also have been in close proximity to Artorias's tomb. The Watchers gained notoriety due to their scorched-earth approach to containing outbreaks of the Abyss, destroying kingdoms at the first sign of exposure. Nonetheless, many would enlist as their followers in a bid to partake of wolf's blood and become part of the Undead Legion.

title: Lord's Blade Ciaran
snippet:
She appears to value Artorias a fair bit, stating that he was a dear friend of hers. She looked for him during the fall of Oolacile only to find him dead, put out of his misery by the Chosen Undead. She erected a small grave for him, offering a black lock of hair, likely the one featured on the knight's helm, and mourned him. Upon meeting the champion who had laid him to rest, she asked them to recieve his afflicted soul so she could give him a proper sendoff.

Years later, when Artorias' deeds faded to legend and the township was subsumed by the surrounding forest, her ring could be found clutched by a female corpse behind the hero's gravestone, meaning that the knight tended to his grave until her very end.

title: Humans
snippet: Meanwhile, in a place called Oolacile, the land of golden sorceries, humans loyal to the Gods were convinced by the Darkwraith leader named Kaathe, a primordial serpent loyal to the Pygmy, to raise up a primeval man who had been buried there. He went mad, and his Humanity bubbled over from his uncontrollable rage, mutating him into a dark monster. His Humanity overflowed and consumed the very world around him, generating another Abyss, and corrupting the citizens of Oolacile. Knight Artorias, one of the four knights of Gwyn, would be tasked to face the outbreak of the Abyss, only to be corrupted by it.

title: Ashen One

In the Church of Filianore, the Ashen One finds Judicator Argo who bars the way to Filianore. He will summon Halflight, Spear of the Church to fight the Ashen One.

title: Frozen Eleum Loyce
snippet: After their King was consumed by Chaos, many of Eleum Loyce's faithful knights decided to follow him and put him out of his misery, as his orders were to eliminate each malformed terror that arose from the flame, and they would thus not hesitate even it were their own leader. Sir Fabian led the loyal knights straight into the depths of the Old Chaos to exterminate its terrors one last time, however the mission proved to be a failure and not one of the selfless knights returned. The souls of the knights were taken by Chaos and corrupted, leading them to lose all sense of purpose and being, left in them driven only by the urge of expuning any who might disturb the flames, even if they were former compatriots. With their armor charred and burnt black by fire and still burning in agony they remained as empty shells controlled by the Chaos alongside their once-proud king.  the_painted_world_of_ariandel : Within the Cathedral of the Deep the Ashen One can encounter Slave Knight Gael, a Slave Knight who seeks unkindled ash to aid his Lady. Gael presents the Ashen One with a fragment of the Painted World of Ariandel, which sucks the Ashen One in. Within the painting, the Ashen One encounters Sister Friede and her loyal knight Sir Vilhelm. Friede is an advisor to Ariandel, the painting's creator, and convinced him to allow the painting to rot rather than allow it to be destroyed and replaced by a new one, despite the wishes of many of the painting's denizens. Friede bids the Ashen One to leave, telling them that they do not belong in the Painted World.

title: Berenike Knight
snippet: As the First Flame began to fade, countless among the ranks of the Berenike Knights became Undead and ventured to Lordran. Here they tried to make their way toward Anor Londo through the only possible access: Sen's Fortress. The knights of Berenike and Tarkus thus entered the dangerous proving ground; after decades of struggling to advance, much of the Knights ended up as Hollows, becoming a threat to the other Undead in the location. Tarkus, probably accompanied by some fellow knights, eventually reached the peak of Sen's Fortress and challenged the last trial in the form of the Iron Golem. The mighty knight in black iron armor managed to defeat the guardian of Anor Londo, gaining access to the city of the gods. However, after reaching Anor Londo, Tarkus perished at the hands of the Painting Guardians before he could reach Gwynevere and obtain the Lordvessel. The few Berenike Knights that followed him to Anor Londo ended up inside the Painted World of Ariamis.

title: The Nameless King
snippet: However, the rest of the firstborn's reign was marked by catastrophes. The Four Kings of New Londo were corrupted by the dark power of Darkstalker Kaathe, starting to sow devastation nearby the city of the gods. Following Knight Artorias's failure to defeat the Darkwraiths, the gods were forced to flood the city, sacrificing all the humans within, and seal it. A similar event happened in Oolacile when, again due to Kaathe, the awakening of the primordial human Manus and his fury led to the collapse of the country when Artorias was unable to defeat him. In addition to the grave situation on the borders of Anor Londo, the city of the gods itself became a dangerous place when a group of cultists began targeting the clan of Gwyn and their kind, and occult weapons capable of killing the gods reached inside the walls of Anor Londo. title: Alva, Seeker of the Spurned
snippet:
This, however, was not the end for the Seeker of the Spurned, now nameless, as he is later encountered in the Ringed City of legend, long after the events of Irithyll Dungeon. It seems that his journey had ended there, where he had finally found the one he was looking for. Unfortunately, his beloved had been dead all along, and the knight could do nothing more than protect her resting place from anyone who'd dare loot her remains. Once again the Ashen One would battle the knight, conquering the ordeal and slaying him for good.

However, the White-Faced Locusts preach of a way for the lovers to be reunited in the Abyss, though their words are hard to fully trust.

However this horrid spirit was eventually defeated by one of the noblest knights. Although it was killed, the strength of the creature did not waver and its spirit was captured into a magic ring with its eye that kept its life-absorbing power.

title: Furtive Pygmy
snippet:
Sometime before the arrival of the Ashen One at the Ringed City, a pygmy—plausibly a disgruntled Pygmy Lord— came to detest the Gods for condemning the pygmies to their accursed fate, and took up residence at the outskirts of their city. There, he welcomed new arrivals and directed into Filianore's Church those who sought the Dark Soul, where they could confront the "lid covering an overgrown privy".

The Pygmy Lords obeyed and relied on the gods for eons, and remained passive unto the end of time, at which point even their own blood had dried up. The last Pygmy Lords would meet their ends at the hands of Slave Knight Gael, who had sought their Dark Soul for centuries. Finding that their blood had long ago dried up, he consumed their Dark Soul, so that he could take it back to his Lady to be used as pigment for her painting.

title: Lord's Blade Ciaran
snippet:
Lord's Blade Ciaran -  Dark Souls III - character - plot 
 plot : Ciaran appears after Artorias is defeated, asking the player for the soul they recieved after the fight. If they decide to hand it over to her, she rewards the player with the Gold Tracer and the Dark Silver Tracer. Refusing to give it to her will prompt her to stay until the area is reloaded, giving the player a chance to change their mind. Once she leaves though, there won't be any way to go back on her offer.

She will not spawn if the player consumes the Soul of Artorias before returning to the arena. The grave will still be there, though no one will be attending it. It's slightly different in the PC Version, as Ciaran can still be found kneeling by the small grave after the soul was used to craft the Abyss Greatsword. This gives the player a chance to still interact with her, or even challenge her for the unique loot such as her set, which cannot be obtained in any other way.

title: Mirrah
snippet: Another traditional order was that of the Shadow Knights which focused on assassinations in the cover of darkness. They quietly carried out unspeakable tasks via any means necessary, using peculiar Shadow Daggers, formed by bending a sword into the shape of a dagger, and black armor to hide in the cover of the night. These knights also employed sorceries like Fall Control and Hush to facilitate their surreptitious activity. The most adept Shadow Knights were also often hired as bodyguards. Some of these assassins at some point fled the order of shadow knights, rejecting all forms of honor, and resorted to unseemly mercenary work.

After Artorias' death, Alvina moved to the ruins of Oolacile, now overgrown and known as the "Darkroot Garden", where the knight had succumbed in his fight against the Abyss of Manus. Sif too had moved here after he survived the battle with Manus and inherited Artorias' divine greatsword and the magical ring that had allowed the knight to cross into the Abyss. The wolf settled in the forest where Artorias' tomb had been erected and, wielding his companion's sword in his jaws, continued to fight to guard Artorias' rest, slaughtering the numerous Undead intent on plundering the tomb of the legendary knight.

title: Nashandra
snippet:
Nashandra -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : Nashandra began her life as a small fragment of Manus, Father of the Abyss. When Manus was defeated, he was reborn as many fragments varying in sizes. Nashandra was the incarnation of her "father's" want, and thus began desiring what she did not have: power.

Nashandra travelled to the land of Drangleic, and set her sights on its powerful ruler, King Vendrick. Deciding to seduce Vendrick, Nashandra assumed a human form of unparalleled beauty and warned him of a supposed looming threat beyond the sea: the Giants. She convinced him to invade the land of the giants to claim their power, which Vendrick did successfully. Vendrick then made Nashandra his queen, and under their leadership, Drangleic entered into a Dark-like peace. The rulership of Drangleic however, was not enough to quell Nashandra’s want, and she desired an even greater power: the First Flame, which she intended to claim for herself by using Vendrick and the Throne of Want.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet: Along with the "elite" Abyss Watchers, the complete Undead Legion consisted of two other levels. The Abyss Watchers recruited acolytes for assistance, who provided support via miracles, sorceries, and other concoctions. At some point, they made a pact of uncertain terms with one of the Crystal Sages of the kingdom of Lothric, who agreed to come to their headquarters in Farron and train their acolytes in sorcerous arts. Due to the Legion's emphasis of speed over physical power, they asked the skilled sorcerer to develop unique variations of existing sorceries for the acolytes to use. At this point, the Watcher's sword will ignite, causing it to deal additional Fire damage and leaving trails in the floor that erupt into large pillars of flame. The Watcher himself will also take on an Embered appearance, revealing his true form as one of the Lords of Cinder.

The other Watchers no longer rise during the second phase, but the main Watcher is considerably more aggressive and powerful. The fight plays out in a similar fashion, but most of the Watcher's greatsword attacks are altered in some way. Killing the Watcher at this point will end the fight, but dying will reset it entirely, requiring the player to beat the first phase again.

 lead : The **Abyss Watchers**, also known as the **Undead Legion of Farron**, are a collective boss in *Dark Souls III*, and are the first of the four main enemies that the Ashen One is tasked with slaying.

Found at the end of Farron Keep, the first phase of their boss battle is unusual: it involves a "main" Watcher whose health bar must be depleted, and who is joined as time passes by others with their own health bars, but also Watchers corrupted by the Abyss, who will indiscriminately target both the Ashen One and the uncorrupted Watchers, the latter of whom will fight back, turning the fight at times into a three-sided battle. Once the main Watcher's health is depleted, they regenerate for a second phase where they are the sole opponent.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet:
Perhaps the most telling of their fall were the number of foot soldiers tasked with the covert disposal of corrupted members. As the Abyss slowly morphed the Legion's lost members, the so-called "Followers" would be sent to execute them before they were transformed into abyssal beasts. Their primary technique was to surround the target, burning and stabbing them, and finishing them with honor using javelins thrown with great force.

Beneath their home in Farron Keep are the Catacombs of Carthus, which contain a chalice holding High Lord Wolnir, who fell to the Abyss long ago. Along with the cindered Smouldering Lake, nearby is the Cathedral of the Deep, resting place of Aldrich, Devourer of Gods.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet: Eventually, the Watchers linked the Fire, although it is unknown if one or all had done so. With the Watchers becoming Lords of Cinder, the wolf blood dried up. The Followers, now having nothing to live for, went hollow, roaming the land and eventually disappearing into the Painted World of Ariandel. With no one remaining to execute the corrupted, the acolytes were slowly devolved by the Abyss, and Farron was consumed in a rotting bog. When the Abyss Watchers were awakened to kindle the Flame once again, they returned home to find it corrupted and their mission unsuccessful. The Watchers in the keep now fight against themselves, endlessly slaying their brethren corrupted by the Abyss.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet:
Abyss Watchers -  Dark Souls III - boss - description 
 description : The Abyss Watchers are a legion of troops that all wear a distinctive armor consisting of leather over chainmail, a long cloak, and a distinctive, pointed helm concealing a mask, seen as a sinister symbol by the masses. They are known for combating the Abyss wherever it may break out, and eradicating any of its abominations. They are believed to serve in the name of Artorias the Abysswalker, who was sworn to the same duty.

All of them use a greatsword and curved dagger. The dagger is not primarily used for offense, or even parrying, but as a hook for the Watchers to utilize their wild, unpredictable fighting style.

By the time the Ashen One encounters the Legion, they are mercilessly fighting one another, seemingly because some of the remaining Watchers have gone mad from exposure to the Abyss, hence their glowing red eyes.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet:
Abyss Watchers -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategy 
 strategy : The fight consists of the player fighting a lone Abyss Watcher, who is present during the entire battle. More Abyss Watchers will awaken to join the battle as it progresses. These Watchers are much more fragile than the main Watcher, but they can still deal a considerable amount of damage, especially when multiple attack at once.

Every other Watcher that awakens, starting from the second, will be red-eyed and hostile toward other Watchers. They can directly attack the player or each other, but they will mostly focus on the other watchers. These Watchers can be used to the player's advantage, as they assist in dealing damage and taking aggro. As such, it may be a good idea to switch to a more defensive playstyle while the player waits for these Watchers to even out the odds.

snippet:

All Watchers are instantly killed when the first phase of the fight is finished.
The Abyss-corrupted (red-eyed) Watchers are capable of finishing off the main Watcher. This has no direct effect on gameplay, however.
If an enemy followed the player up to the fog door, it may attract the corrupted Watcher's attention and he will keep trying to attack it for the rest of the first phase, rendering him unable to help against the others.
The Watchers that resurrect in the first phase of the fight are actually the same two Watchers, they will resurrect on the spot where they were killed.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet: The main Watcher, although carrying a greatsword, is extremely fast and dexterous. He is constantly jumping around and evading the players swings by doing so. He will also try to take an advantage by swinging his greatsword around the floor of the arena. Never let your guard down, each and every attack can take you by surprise.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet:
Though the Legion was not inherently evil or overtly violent, they quickly became known for their scorched-earth tactics, said to "bury" entire kingdoms at the first sign of exposure. Their distinct outfits, topped off with a tall, pointed helm, became an ill omen for its beholders. Their fighting style was enhanced by the revolutionary use of an ultra greatsword—modeled after Artorias' sword—along with a carved dagger, utilizing the dagger as support for utilizing their own unique, highly agile fighting techniques that was even more unpredictable and vicious than their predecessor. As such, they disdained the use of shields and preferred a constant offense.

The wolf's blood did more than enhance their bodies; the very essence of each Watcher who partook of the blood was interlinked, coalescing their souls into one. As such, instead of each body hosting distinct souls, all that partook the wolf blood shared the one soul, that of the "wolf blood master", distributed amongst them.

snippet:
Dusk of Oolacile -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Dusk appears to believe that she was saved by Artorias, as told by the legend, while in actuality she was saved by the Chosen Undead. While unaware that Artorias had been corrupted by the Abyss before he could save her, Dusk's senses do hint that the Chosen Undead bears the same "resonance" as her fabled savior, leading her to question the details of her temporarily intangible captivity.
The feelings that she sensed during her imprisonment in the Abyss—"*a wrenching nostalgia, a lost joy, an object of obsession, and a sincere hope to reclaim it"—*are evocative of the "shards" of Manus present in Drangleic, who each represented a form of longing; namely Nadalia, Alsanna, Nashandra and Elana.

title: Great Grey Wolf Sif
snippet:
Despite sharing a name with a Norse goddess, Sif's gender is unconfirmed, and is not directly stated in either the English or Japanese versions of the game.
**In translations for languages that have grammatical gender, the masculine form of "wolf" is often used when referring to Sif. In French, Sif is called *Le Grand Loup Gris*, using the masculine "loup" rather than the feminine "louve", In Spanish, Sif is called *El Gran Lobo Gris*, using the masculine "lobo" rather than the feminine "loba", In Russian, Sif is called *Великий Волк*, using the masculine "волк" rather than the feminine "волчица", In Italian, Sif is called *Il Grande Lupo Grigio*, using the masculine "lupo" rather than the feminine "lupa".
**In the strategy guide by FuturePress, Sif is referred using masculine pronouns.
Another possible naming influence is the Arabic *saif* or *sayf*, meaning "sword".

title: Great Grey Wolf Sif
snippet:
Using miracles, sorcery, or pyromancy to soften Sif up before moving in with melee attacks can also prove to be effective.
Using a summoned phantom as a decoy can make positioning oneself under Sif easier. In a party of two or more players only one should try to get under Sif, otherwise players may bump into each other when trying to dodge Sif's attacks.
Sif's attacks can be blocked, but most of them will cause a significant loss of stamina, even with a good shield. Learning Sif's attack patterns and avoiding them completely, either by dodging or simply walking out of the way, is highly recommended.

title: Great Grey Wolf Sif
snippet:
Great Grey Wolf Sif -  Dark Souls - boss - strategies 
 strategies : For melee fighters, getting underneath Sif is generally the best strategy, as it makes most attacks miss the player character completely. Care must still be taken to dodge, block or move out of the way of the slam attack, though. Locking on is not always a good idea when doing this, as it can make the camera spin and make it harder to control one's position. Two-handing is more effective, as it will make the fight shorter and reduce the number of slams that need to be dodged.
For ranged characters, players can simply target-lock Sif and kite Sif backwards around the edge of the arena. Staying as far as possible away from Sif will cause most, if not all, of Sif's attacks to miss.
Using miracles, sorcery, or pyromancy to soften Sif up before moving in with melee attacks can also prove to be effective.

title: Great Grey Wolf Sif
snippet:
Great Grey Wolf Sif -  Dark Souls - boss - trivia 
 trivia : In Norse mythology, Sif is the golden-haired wife of the god Thor.
** The goddess Sif's name in Old Norse is pronounced /siːf/, "seef", though it is often anglicized to /sɪf/, "siff". It is also a female given name in modern day Iceland.
**The name "Sif" is believed to be a singular form derived from Old Norse *sifjar*, "connection by marriage". The modern English "sib", as in "sibling", comes from the same root, as does the German "Sippe", meaning "tribe" or, coloquially, "family".
** In *Advanced Dungeons & Dragons* sourcebook *Legends & Lore* (1984), the goddess Sif is depicted wielding a longsword and wearing white and silver. These traits are shared with the Dark Souls boss Sif.
Despite sharing a name with a Norse goddess, Sif's gender is unconfirmed, and is not directly stated in either the English or Japanese versions of the game.

title: Great Grey Wolf Sif
snippet:
**In the strategy guide by FuturePress, Sif is referred using masculine pronouns.
Another possible naming influence is the Arabic *saif* or *sayf*, meaning "sword".
In Japanese, Sif is named 灰色の大狼シフ (*Haiiro no Ookami Shifu*), meaning "Grey (literally "ash-colored") Wolf Sif". "Ookami", "wolf", is often written in Japanese with 狼 alone (such as in the Japanese title of the anime *Spice and Wolf*, 狼と香辛料), but here is written 大狼, also read "ookami", with the first kanji carrying the meaning "great" or "large". 大狼 is also used in the Japanese translations of *A Song of Ice and Fire* to refer to the direwolves, though in that series it is read ダイアウルフ (katakana for the English "direwolf"). The alternative reading "Dairou" for 大狼 has been suggested, but this is not attested in the game.
In the fight against the Chosen Undead, Sif wields the sword of Artorias, former companion who sacrificed himself in order to protect Sif.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: Sometime after Lord Gwyn sacrificed himself to link the fading First Flame, the Primordial Serpent Kaathe began searching for a human strong enough to become the Dark Lord capable of leading humans and usher in an Age of Dark. Kaathe eventually arrived in New Londo and managed to entice the Four Kings, powerful humans who had received a fragment of Gwyn's Lord Soul, into following his ideals, teaching them the art of Lifedrain. The Serpent's dark influence extended to their entire army: The knights of New Londo became Darkwraiths, servants of the Dark who learned the art of Lifedrain and used it to absorb humanity. The Four Kings opened an Abyss in the center of their city, with their Darkwraiths beginning to employ the Red Eye Orbs granted by Kaathe to plunder humanity and expand the reach of the Abyss.
